the policy needs $\geq$\,2.0. \emph{Queue} is the 20\,\% reserve left after the
third aircraft's 120\,s hold plus two 53\,s descents.}\\[3pt]

\vspace{10pt}
{\large\bfseries\color{accent} Open before ordering}
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=14pt,itemsep=2pt,topsep=3pt]
\item \textbf{Battery: weigh it.} GenX publishes no mass; 1880--2211\,g is bracketed from 165--194\,Wh/kg. The cost of 16\,Ah is thrust-to-weight: 1.8--1.9 on the same motors unless the stand shows $\geq$\,3.55\,kgf per motor. Charge it as LiHV. Its AS150 plug needs AS150 mates, not XT90S. The 150\,A fuse is now the tightest margin against a $\sim$136\,A peak.
\item \textbf{Failsafe parameters.} \texttt{params.py} and the pack model still describe the Li-ion pack. Once the LiPo arrives, measure its sag curve, then update both. Do not fly before that.
\item \textbf{ESC.} The 65\,A is a candidate. It is confirmed on the thrust stand for current, temperature and desync with 18\,in props and 340\,KV motors.
\item \textbf{Base antenna cable.} 3\,m of RG58, 50\,$\Omega$, TNC-male to SMA-male, made by a local RF cable shop. The INR~600 is an estimate, so get the quote before ordering.
\item \textbf{Ground antennas.} Each receiver gets a 14\,dBi panel aimed at its own aircraft, plus an omni on its second port: wfb-ng transmits from the ground too, so neither port can be left open. Aim the panels and confirm the polarisation, which the listing does not state. The listed range is for analog FPV, not wfb-ng. Coax lengths depend on the ground-station layout.
\item \textbf{USB hub.} Check the adapter's rating when it arrives.
\item \textbf{Confirmed:} the GenX F9P Air is dual-band (GPS L1/L2, Galileo E1/E5b, BDS B1/B2, GLONASS G1/G2), with a QMC5883 compass.
\end{itemize}
